Furthermore, the rupee showed notable strength, closing below the 95-mark for the first time in 38 days, reflecting the effective measures implemented by the Reserve Bank of India.

Better-than-expected September quarter earnings mirroring Accenture's stellar performance and robust future guidance, steady deal flows, and inexpensive valuations after a spell of prolonged correction drew investors back to the sector that is typically over-owned by overseas funds. ET Bureau The Nifty IT index surged 11.7% during the week, its biggest gain for the period since April 2008, even as semiconductor-heavy Asian markets tumbled amid concerns over the profitability of massive AI investments. "The rally is being driven by better-than-expected quarterly results, particularly from HCLTech, improving deal prospects and value buying after a prolonged correction," said Ravi Singh, chief research officer at Master Capital Services. India's IT services sector is also showing signs of stabilisation after nearly two years of cost-cutting and subdued growth. Growth averaged 2-2.5% quarter-on-quarter, while rupee-reported revenue rose 11-15% year-on-year. TCS onboarded 24,000 freshers in the first half of the year, while HCLTech added 6,450 employees during the quarter. Live Events The technology index jumped 3.9% to close at 31,924 on Friday, its highest level since February 22. To be sure, even after the latest surge, the index has retreated 16% year-to-date. The Nifty gained 2.8% during the week. "It certainly feels like the narrative in the market is a little bit jittery," said Garrett Melson, portfolio strategist with Natixis Investment Managers Solutions. "Clearly there's a lot of uncertainty around where AI stands right now." Worries rippled through markets over risks tied to the financing of the AI build-out boom, which has lifted profits for a wide swath of companies and boosted economic growth. Investors were watching developments with CoreWeave, an AI cloud company with about $50 billion in debt. This week, its shares tumbled. Live Events In other recent signs of caution, strategists at Deutsche Bank and RBC Capital Markets separately pulled back on their recommendations of the tech sector. On October 9, Deutsche Bank strategists said the rotation into tech had "run far and the risk-reward no longer looks favorable in the near term." Dragged down by the swoon in heavyweight tech and AI stocks, the S&P 500 posted its biggest weekly drop since June. But the benchmark index was only about 2% below its record high set this month. Read Today's Paper Jio’s $3.2 billion IPO tests Ambani appeal with young Indians SECTIONS Jio’s $3.2 billion IPO tests Ambani appeal with young Indians By Hemal Savai, Ashutosh Joshi , Bloomberg Last Updated: Oct 17, 2026, 09:18:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Bloomberg For generations of Indians, Reliance Industries Ltd. was their introduction to the stock market. Founder Dhirubhai Ambani drew middle-income savers into shares, building a following that endured for decades. Nearly fifty years after Reliance went public, his billionaire son Mukesh and grandson Akash are preparing to list the group’s telecom and digital services arm in what is set to be India’s biggest initial public offering. Jio Platforms Ltd. plans to raise about $3.2 billion in the offering, which opens on Oct. 21. The IPO will test how much the Reliance brand still matters to retail investors. Jio is pitching to a very different market from the one Dhirubhai knew. India now has more than 130 million registered stock-market investors, nearly 40% of them under 30, according to National Stock Exchange of India data. Thousands of stocks, a vast array of mutual funds and other assets compete for their money. Older shareholders regarded Reliance as a stock they could hold for decades. For younger investors, growth, profits and valuation play a bigger role in the investment decision. Mahendra Chheda, 69, started as a floor trader in the late 1960s before becoming a member of the Bombay Stock Exchange. “Be it Dhirubhai’s ambition, his quest to create an army of retail investors or the return of capital to shareholders, Reliance set itself miles apart,” he said. His son, Hardik, 44, an equities trader, takes a different view of Jio. Live Events “I will be taking out profit soon after listing,” he said. “Retail investors owe a lot to the Ambanis for popularizing direct stock ownership, but we are now in a different era of financial markets.” Reliance, under Mukesh’s leadership, has grown from a maker of textiles and chemicals into India’s most valuable company with businesses spanning energy, consumer goods and telecom. Under Dhirubhai, a first-generation entrepreneur who challenged Mumbai’s entrenched industrial establishment, the company decided to tap thousands of individual investors to help set up his textile empire. The November 1977 IPO raised 28 million rupees and drew about 58,000 investors, with the offering subscribed seven times, according to Reliance’s annual report. It helped fuel what became known as India’s ‘equity cult,’ as more households began buying shares directly. Annual shareholder meetings grew into mass gatherings, including one held at Cooperage Football Ground in south Mumbai in the mid-1980s. Reliance shares have delivered an annualized average return of about 29% since listing, according to a presentation at a Mumbai roadshow on Thursday. This year, however, the stock has fallen 23% amid a broader selloff in local equities, putting it on track for its worst annual performance since 2011. The Nifty began the week on a positive note and extended its recovery, although the broader technical setup remained challenging. The Index traded in a range of 861.40 points. Weekly volatility cooled by 2.23% to 14.06. The headline Index eventually ended the week with a net gain of 625.70 points (+2.78%). The most significant technical development of the week was Nifty reclaiming its 200-week Moving Average, currently at 22,651.47, after slipping below it in the preceding weeks. This recovery is significant because it has, at least for now, prevented a deeper deterioration in the Index's long-term technical structure. The 200-week MA has historically served as an important reference point for the primary trend, and the Nifty's ability to move back above it has reduced the immediate risk of a structural breakdown. However, this recovery should not yet be interpreted as a confirmed trend reversal. The Index continues to trade below its 20-week, 50-week, and 100-week moving averages, indicating that significant overhead resistance remains in place. The immediate challenge is for the Nifty to sustain above the 200-week MA and build on the recovery. ET CONTRIBUTORS The coming week is likely to see markets attempting to consolidate the previous week's gains. The 23,300 and 23,550 levels are likely to act as immediate resistance. Support comes in at 22,950 and 22,650. The trading week will also be truncated, with Tuesday, October 20, a trading holiday due to Dussehra. The weekly RSI stands at 42.29. The move follows a review of the Closing Auction Session. Sebi is also working on simpler regulations, easier market access, lower compliance costs and stronger technological resilience. THE ECONOMIC TIMES The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. The Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi ) is likely to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within about a week, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. The regulator is examining feedback on its consultation paper following a review of the Closing Auction Session (CAS). “Following review of the Closing Auction Session, a consultation paper was put out to address concerns in respect of settlement price of derivatives on expiry-day. We are currently examining the comments and hope to issue guidelines in about a week’s time,” Pandey said at the second Capital Market Confluence 2026, organised by the Bombay Stock Exchange Brokers’ Forum in Mumbai. The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. Pandey said wider participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and efficient hedging and arbitrage could help improve liquidity and the functioning of cash markets. In his address, titled “From Regulation to Global Leadership: Positioning India’s Capital Markets as a Standard-Setter for the Next Decade”, the Sebi chairman outlined four broad priorities for the market regulator: proportionate regulation, deeper cash markets, easier access to Indian markets and greater technological resilience. On the regulatory front, Pandey said Sebi was reviewing the Depositories and Participants Regulations to simplify rules and strengthen fraud prevention. The regulator is also exploring a graded compliance framework for stock brokers based on their scale, client exposure and dependence on technology. Live Events “One size need not fit all,” he said. Sebi is also addressing gaps in the interoperability framework for certain transactions, including tender offers, buybacks and offers for sale (OFS). These transactions currently require parallel clearing arrangements, adding to costs and compliance requirements, Pandey said. The regulator is targeting implementation of the proposed changes by the end of November 2026. The move is expected to improve capital efficiency and lower compliance costs while preserving settlement safety, he said. Legendary value investor Michael Price believed successful investing requires independent thinking, rigorous research and the discipline to look beyond short-term market movements. His investment philosophy focused on identifying companies trading below their intrinsic value , particularly businesses facing temporary financial difficulties that have the potential to recover. Price developed much of his approach under the guidance of veteran investor Max Heine of Mutual Series Mutual Funds. Over the years, he built a reputation for investing in undervalued companies and identifying opportunities that other market participants may overlook. Look beyond cheap valuations Price believed a low share price or an inexpensive valuation does not automatically make a stock an attractive investment. Foreign investors sell Indian equities worth Rs 45,000 crore in just 6 sessions. What can reverse the trend? FII selloff has intensified in October, with foreign investors net selling Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in just six sessions in October so far, nearly the same as the total Rs 45,536 crore outflows recorded in the entire month of September. Analysts have listed factors that could change the trend and ease pressure on the market. The Indian stock market snapped a record eight-week-long losing streak last week, ending with gains despite strong upswings and downswings. Yet, FIIs remained bearish and continued selling Indian equities in every session so far in October. The foreign investors have remained net sellers of Indian equities for 11 consecutive sessions since mid-September. What's behind the massive FII outflows? The sharp FII selloff came as bond yields soared to multi-year highs, making the risk-free returns from the debt market more lucrative than equities. The 10-year US Treasury yield recorded its biggest quarterly increase of the 21st century in the three months ended September, Reuters reported. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries climbed above 5.3%, surpassing its 2007 peak and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that the rapid acceleration in FII outflows in October so far has taken the total FPI equity selling in 2026 to a whopping Rs 3,60,952 crore. “This massive FPI selling is the primary reason why the Indian market is underperforming this year with negative 13.87% Nifty returns so far in 2026,” he said. Live Events Also read | D-St Exit Rush! Sectors that saw sharpest FII selloff in 2nd half of September When can the trend reverse? From the FPI perspective, the rationale behind the massive outflows is the risk-free return from the 10-year US bonds being above 5.2%, according to the analyst. “So long as the US bond yields remain elevated, FPIs will continue to sell. The scenario will change when the valuations become attractive, and the risk-reward ratio turns favourable for investment,” Vijayakumar explained. Shares of Swan Defence and Heavy Industries rose 4.1% to Rs 2,850 on BSE on Monday after the company emerged as the lowest bidder for a Rs 1,897 crore order to build four medium-range product tankers for a proposed joint venture led by state-run Shipping Corporation of India (SCI). The potential contract would strengthen the shipbuilder's order book as India looks to revive domestic shipbuilding after a gap of 25 years in locally built oil tankers. The stock touched an intraday high of Rs 2,874.55, which was also its 52-week high and the upper price band for the day. The company quoted around $48.9 million per vessel when price bids were opened on Friday, October 9, beating state-run Cochin Shipyard Ltd, which quoted around $4 million more per vessel. Swan Defence's tanker opportunity after 25 years The proposed order involves two firm and two optional dual-fuel-ready medium-range product tankers, each capable of carrying 17,000-18,000 tonnes of cargo. The contract, once signed, would mark the first attempt in a quarter of a century to build oil tankers locally. Swan Defence has a technical tie-up with Samsung Heavy Industries, one of South Korea's top three shipbuilders. ETMarkets.com ICICI Pru AMC Q2 Results: The company's mutual fund quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) rose 14.4% YoY to Rs 11.61 lakh crore ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company on Monday reported a 6.1% year-on-year (YoY) rise in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 889 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 838 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. The company’s board also declared an interim dividend of Rs 30 per equity share and fixed October 21, 2026, as the record date for determining eligible shareholders. Revenue from operations rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 1,674 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 1,439 crore in Q2 FY26. Total expenses increased 17.9% to Rs 493 crore during the quarter, from Rs 418 crore a year earlier. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, the company reported a 14.3% YoY increase in PAT to Rs 1,854 crore, compared with Rs 1,622 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. ICICI Prudentia AMC's mutual fund quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) rose 14.4% YoY to Rs 11.61 lakh crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, from Rs 10.15 lakh crore a year earlier. Its market share stood at 13.3%. The segment had a market share of 13.3%. Assets in equity and equity-oriented schemes rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 6.59 lakh crore, from Rs 5.67 lakh crore, with a market share of 13.7%. Equity-oriented hybrid schemes recorded a 19.7% increase in QAAUM to Rs 2.29 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.91 lakh crore a year earlier. The segment’s market share stood at 26.4%. In its alternatives business, QAAUM stood at Rs 80,965 crore as of September 30, 2026. This included Rs 30,791 crore in portfolio management services (PMS), Rs 24,260 crore in alternative investment funds (AIFs) and Rs 25,914 crore in assets under advisory. Read Today's Paper Polycab India’s F&O exit: NSE sets December 30 deadline; NCLAT stays insolvency order SECTIONS Polycab India’s F&O exit: NSE sets December 30 deadline; NCLAT stays insolvency order By Kumar Gaurav , Last Updated: Oct 12, 2026, 09:54:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis NSE will remove Polycab India from the equity derivatives segment from December 30, 2026, with existing contracts available until expiry. Separately, NCLAT has stayed the NCLT order admitting insolvency proceedings against the company over an alleged Rs 2.79 crore operational debt, pending further orders. ETMarkets.com No contracts for new expiry months in Polycab India will be issued after the expiry of existing contract months. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) will exclude Polycab India from the equity derivatives segment with effect from December 30, 2026, according to an exchange's latest circular. The NSE circular stated that no contracts for new expiry months in Polycab India will be issued after the expiry of existing contract months. However, existing unexpired contracts for October, November and December 2026 will continue to be available for trading until their respective expiry dates. New strikes will also be introduced in these existing contract months. No contracts in Polycab India will be available for trading in the equity derivatives segment from December 30, 2026, the exchange said. ALSO READ: Market Trading Guide: Astra Microwave, Manappuram among 5 stock recommendations for Tuesday Separately, Polycab India informed the exchanges that NCLAT had stayed and kept in abeyance the October 7 order passed by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Ahmedabad Bench, admitting the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) against the company in a case filed by Asier Metals Private Limited. Live Events The proceedings relate to an alleged operational debt of Rs 2.79 crore under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. According to the NCLAT order, counsel for Polycab submitted that a pre-existing dispute existed between the parties concerning payments made and credit notes to be issued by the operational creditor. The company's counsel also submitted that Polycab was willing to deposit the entire amount stated in Part IV of the insolvency application, without prejudice to its rights and contentions. The tribunal directed that the amount be deposited through a fixed deposit receipt (FDR) in the name of the Registrar, NCLAT, New Delhi, within a week. It stayed the NCLT's October 7 order and kept it in abeyance until further orders. Polycab India shares settled 1.82% higher at Rs 8,405 apiece on the NSE on Monday, compared with the previous close of Rs 8,255. During the session, the stock traded between Rs 8,291 and Rs 8,469. The stock has gained nearly 10% so far in 2026, while the Nifty 50 has declined nearly 14% over the same period, according to the data provided. Read Today's Paper Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% SECTIONS Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 13, 2026, 06:15:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Tata Elxsi reported a 10% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 170 crore in Q2, while revenue from operations grew 15% to Rs 1,056 crore. Higher employee and operating expenses, along with lower other income, weighed on margins. Net profit for the first half of FY27 rose 14%. ETMarkets.com Tata Elxsi on Tuesday reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the September quarter, helped by double-digit growth in revenue even as higher employee and operating costs kept profit growth below the top-line expansion. The company’s net profit for the quarter ended September stood at Rs 170 crore, compared with Rs 155 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations rose 15% YoY to Rs 1,056 crore from Rs 918 crore a year earlier. Total income from operations, including other income, increased 13% to Rs 1,090 crore, compared with Rs 967 crore a year earlier. Other income fell to Rs 35 crore from Rs 49 crore, partly weighing on the overall profit growth. Profit before tax rose 11% to Rs 239 crore from Rs 215 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total tax expense increased to Rs 69 crore from Rs 60 crore. There was no exceptional item in the quarter. The company’s total expenses grew 13% YoY to Rs 851 crore from Rs 752 crore. Employee benefit expenses, the largest cost item for the company, rose 15% to Rs 620 crore from Rs 539 crore. Other expenses also increased 15% to Rs 131 crore from Rs 114 crore. Cost of materials consumed rose marginally to Rs 73 crore from Rs 72 crore. Depreciation and amortisation expense stood at Rs 24 crore, compared with Rs 23 crore a year earlier. Finance costs declined to Rs 3.57 crore from Rs 4 crore. Live Events Also read: Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPO The company’s profit before tax margin on revenue from operations stood at 22.7%, compared with 23.4% a year earlier. Net profit margin also moderated to 16.1% from 16.9%, reflecting the impact of higher costs and lower other income. Net profit for the six-month period increased 14% to Rs 341 crore, compared with Rs 299 crore in the same period last year. Profit before tax for the April-September period rose 15% to Rs 472 crore from Rs 411 crore. Total income from operations stood at Rs 2,153 crore, up 13% from Rs 1,897 crore a year earlier. NSE IFSC Ltd and the London Stock Exchange have signed a memorandum of understanding to explore strategic collaboration across listings, trading, new products and market connectivity, in a move aimed at strengthening capital-market links between India’s GIFT City and London. The agreement, announced at GIFT IFSC in Gandhinagar on October 13, will allow the two exchanges to explore opportunities for dual and cross-listings across equities, fixed income and exchange-traded funds. The partnership will also look at trading in existing financial products and the development of new products, including derivatives on NSEIX using FTSE Russell indices as underlying references. The MoU also covers possible joint development of new equity indices, cross-border trading connectivity and market-data distribution. The framework is exploratory at this stage, but it signals a deeper push to connect Indian issuers and investors with London’s capital market ecosystem. For NSEIX, the pact comes at a time when GIFT City is being developed as India’s international financial services hub. The exchange already offers a range of products, including Indian single-stock derivatives, index derivatives, currency derivatives, depository receipts and global stocks. It also provides primary-market products such as equity share listings, SPACs, REITs, InvITs, depository receipts, debt securities and ESG debt securities under the IFSCA framework. Live Events V Balasubramaniam, MD and CEO of NSEIX, said the collaboration had emerged from the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, which is aimed at opening new areas in capital-market connectivity and financial-services integration between London and India. "The LSEG London Stock Exchange and NSEIX have taken this first step towards collaborations through dual listings and cross listings across products and exploring a cross-border connect between the two exchanges to provide seamless bidirectional trading opportunities, leading to higher liquidity and a larger pool of investors," Balasubramaniam said. Sign In What's Included Exclusive Stories Daily ePaper Access Smart Market Tools Curated Investment Ideas Ad-lite Experience Subscription ANI The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has invited public comments on recommendations to review the framework for monitoring and disclosure of utilisation of issue proceeds by listed companies . The regulator sought comments on the recommendations of a working group constituted to review the Sebi (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 (LODR Regulations). Stakeholders can submit their comments and suggestions, along with the rationale, by November 3, 2026, in its latest circular. The working group, chaired by V S Sundaresan, former executive director at Sebi, was constituted to review the LODR Regulations with the aim of streamlining the rules and simplifying their structure and language. The paper said the group was constituted "to streamline the regulations, simplify the structure and language, remove ambiguities and redundancy, etc." The working group has submitted its first report, which comprises three chapters. The first deals with monitoring and disclosure of utilisation of issue proceeds, the second covers penal provisions and actions by stock exchanges for non-compliance by listed companies, and the third addresses clarifications on related-party transaction provisions. Live Events ALSO READ: Sebi extends easier IPO rules till March 2027 The LODR Regulations were published in the Gazette of India on September 2, 2015. The objective was "to consolidate, streamline, and harmonize the various existing listing agreements into a single, unified framework and strengthen corporate governance, transparency, and protection of the interests of investors." The regulator noted that the regulations have been amended periodically since 2015, which "may have led to various interpretation issues arising out of multiple amendments." The consultation paper also identifies provisions under the Sebi (Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations dealing with monitoring agencies for initial public offerings on the main board, rights issues, further public offers, preferential issues, qualified institutional placements and initial public offerings by small and medium enterprises. In a regulatory filing, the company said its pre-sales rose to Rs 2,136 crore in the second quarter of this fiscal from Rs 1,322 crore in the year-ago period. Sales area for the second quarter stood at 1.83 million square feet, up 22 per cent annually. Average price realisation increased 32 per cent annually to Rs 11,651 per square foot. In the first six months of this fiscal, the company has handed over 1,722 homes spanning 1.92 million sq ft. ETMarkets.com Tata Technologies on Wednesday reported a 4% year-on-year (YoY) rise in second-quarter profit, even as revenue grew at a much faster pace, helped by strong momentum in its services business and continued demand from automotive and manufacturing clients. The company’s net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 stood at Rs 171 crore, compared with Rs 166 crore in the same quarter last year. Operating revenue rose 28% YoY to Rs 1,699 crore, while services segment revenue grew 34% to Rs 1,356 crore. Operating EBITDA increased 32% YoY to Rs 273 crore, with EBITDA margin at 16.1%, up 40 basis points from a year earlier and flat sequentially. Net income margin stood at 10.1%. In dollar terms, services revenue came in at $142 million, up 4.3% quarter-on-quarter in constant currency. The company’s workforce stood at 12,895, while last-twelve-month attrition was 15.6%. Tata Technologies said the quarter reflected sustained growth momentum and resilient margins. The company, which provides product engineering and digital services, works with global manufacturers across automotive, aerospace, industrial heavy machinery and other sectors. Live Events CEO and MD Warren Harris said the strong second-quarter performance reinforced the company’s positive outlook for FY27. He said Tata Technologies remained confident of delivering strong double-digit growth for the full year, supported by robust demand, ongoing programme ramp-ups and healthy pipeline conversion. Harris said the company’s leadership in product realisation, growing full-vehicle development capabilities, expanding aerospace presence and AI-native transformation were helping it become a more differentiated engineering and technology partner. CFO Uttam Gujrati said the 28% revenue growth and 32% EBITDA growth reflected the strength of the company’s diversified portfolio, improving deal momentum and disciplined execution. He said the company continued to face some near-term challenges in certain customer segments and geographies, but the underlying demand environment remained encouraging. The company also announced several deal wins during the quarter. After her recent comments sparked hopes for a tax rejig among investors, analysts noted that such easing would result in FIIs finally making their much-awaited comeback, which in turn would be favourable for the wounded bulls on Dalal Street. Following the 2024 General Elections, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in July announced an overhaul in the way India taxes profits made from the equity stock market. The tax on short-term capital gains (STCG), which essentially are profits booked within one year of purchase, was raised from 15% to 20%, while long-term capital gains tax on equities was increased from 10% to 12.5%. Also read | FM Sitharaman's LTCG tax remarks lift Sensex by 1,100 points. Can markets hope for a review? FII outflows intensified since 2024 Analysts had warned that the changes would spook FIIs out of Dalal Street, and the warning unfortunately came true. Foreign investors net sold Indian equities worth Rs 2,774 crore from July till the end of 2024. Fuelled by multiple headwinds including Trump’s tariff flip-flops, the Middle East war, a weakening rupee and soaring bond yields, the FII sell-off intensified over the years. FII outflows jumped to Rs 1.66 lakh crore in 2025 and Rs 3.06 lakh crore in 2026 so far. Such heavy selling by foreign investors has added to the headwinds pressuring Indian equities following the sharp bull run of 2024.

However, the gains were capped below the 95 per dollar mark as dollar demand linked to importer hedging and portfolio outflows persisted. The rupee climbed to a peak of 94.77 in early trading before settling 0.1% higher at 95.15. "A durable turnaround in the currency will also require negative global triggers to subside. "Should depreciation pressures intensify again, markets are likely to price a higher probability of a front-loaded and more aggressive rate-hike cycle." Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra has defended India's recent forex curbs as an effort to discourage speculative bets and said the central bank is ready to take additional steps to ensure orderly rupee movement. Live Events He added that while monetary policy is not typically deployed to address financial stability concerns, the two cannot be entirely separated. Traders interpreted the remarks as a signal of limited tolerance to further rupee weakness. The South Asian currency had declined over 7% year-to-date before fresh measures over the weekend and has risen 2% this week. Rupee swap markets are currently pricing in nearly 100 bps of rate hikes over the next 12 months. Indian importers continue to lock in future dollar purchase rates to protect against the rupee weakening, despite the banks charging more following the central bank's steps. Investors await US consumer inflation data , due later in the day, for cues on the future path of interest rates in the world's largest economy. The dollar index was last at 102.2. Largecaps , long seen as the core of institutional portfolios, are losing their share of the market even as mid- and smallcap companies expand their footprint. The combined market capitalisation share of mid- and smallcaps reached a record 43.7% in September, while the share of the top 100 companies fell to a low of 56.3%, according to data from Motilal Oswal Financial Services . The shift has been accompanied by a sharp performance gap. In the first half of FY27, the Nifty50 rose just 1.3%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 gained 24.6%, according to Prateek Nigudkar, senior fund manager at Shriram AMC . “The defining feature of the quarter was the sharp divergence between largecaps and the broader market,” Nigudkar said. The divergence, however, is not necessarily a straightforward verdict on fundamentals. It has been shaped significantly by the direction of capital flows. Foreign investors, who typically own a larger share of India’s biggest companies, have been selling largecaps as global bond yields rose, the rupee weakened and oil prices climbed. Domestic institutions, supported by steady systematic investment plan inflows, have directed more money towards mid- and smallcap stocks. “Largecaps, owned heavily by foreign investors, have borne the brunt of global risk-off selling, while smaller companies, owned mostly by domestic investors, have been cushioned by steady SIP inflows,” Nigudkar said. Live Events That flow-driven divergence has created a new market paradox where smaller companies now account for a record share of India’s market, but largecaps are beginning to look more attractive on valuations. Read Today's Paper Sebi revises CAS rules, changes derivatives expiry settlement methodology SECTIONS Sebi revises CAS rules, changes derivatives expiry settlement methodology By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 15, 2026, 09:45:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Sebi has announced changes to the closing auction session for the equity cash market, which will begin in December 2026. The revised session will run from 3.30 pm to 3.40 pm, with specific phases for order entry. Moreover, the methodology for calculating settlement prices for derivatives contracts has been updated. Unexecuted orders will transition under new rules while maintaining time priority differences. Agencies Sebi has revised the rules and norms related to closing auction session and derivatives expiry settlement methodology. Capital markets regulator Sebi has revised the framework for the closing auction session in the equity cash market , including changes to trading timings , the treatment of unexecuted orders and the calculation of settlement prices for derivatives contracts. Under the revised framework, the closing auction session (CAS) will run from 3.30 pm to 3.40 pm on all trading days. The changes will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for modifications governing the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session, which will come into force on February 8, 2027. Sebi introduced the closing auction session to facilitate transparent and efficient price discovery for closing prices of securities. Following its implementation, the regulator reviewed aspects of the framework and sought public comments through a consultation paper issued on September 12. The revised schedule divides the 10-minute auction into three phases. The first minute, starting at 3.30 pm, will be used to calculate the reference price and transition orders from the continuous trading session. Order entry for both limit and market orders will be permitted from 3.31 pm to 3.36 pm, followed by a four-minute period during which only limit orders can be entered. Market orders cannot be modified or cancelled during this final phase. The order-entry window will close randomly between 3.38 pm and 3.40 pm. Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3.45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3.30 pm. Stock derivatives will continue trading until 3.45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash market will run from 3.50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing price of the securities. Live Events The regulator has also revised the methodology for calculating derivatives settlement prices on expiry days. The settlement price of expiring index derivatives will be based on the value of the underlying index calculated using the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of its constituent securities during the final 30 minutes of the continuous trading session in the equity cash market. For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the final 30 minutes of the cash market session across all stock exchanges. Urban Company on Friday reported a net loss of Rs 182 crore in the September quarter, widening from Rs 59 crore a year earlier and Rs 92 crore in the June quarter, as the home services platform stepped up investments in its quick services business, InstaHelp. Revenue from operations rose 41% year-on-year to Rs 537 crore in the second quarter of FY27. Net transaction value (NTV) grew 39% YoY to Rs 1,432 crore, while orders delivered increased 103% YoY to 15.1 million. Annual transacting users rose 35% to nearly 10 million. The company’s consolidated adjusted EBITDA loss stood at Rs 144 crore, reflecting an investment of Rs 174 crore in InstaHelp. Excluding InstaHelp, adjusted EBITDA increased 213% YoY to Rs 30 crore. The company’s board has approved a fresh capital raise of up to Rs 2,500 crore, subject to shareholder approval, to provide financial flexibility for investments across its businesses, strengthen its position in InstaHelp and pursue selective acquisitions. Urban Company had cash and treasury investments of Rs 1,901 crore at the end of the quarter. The company said its consolidated NTV had grown around 40% YoY for three consecutive quarters, supported by new user acquisition, repeat usage and expansion into newer markets. New user acquisition increased 46% YoY over this period. Live Events Penetration in the largest service categories across the top eight cities remains below 10%, while Tier 2 cities recorded NTV growth of around 37% YoY. Its international business grew 66% YoY, while its Native products business is preparing for the festive season in the December quarter. Core business improves margins India Consumer Services, excluding InstaHelp, reported NTV growth of 26.3% YoY to Rs 963 crore. Adjusted EBITDA stood at Rs 34 crore, equivalent to 3.5% of NTV, compared with 2.4% a year earlier, marking an improvement of 110 basis points. Annual transacting users in the segment grew 22.4% YoY to around 8.6 million. First-time users increased around 28% to 0.76 million, while NTV per annual transacting user rose 3.2%. Despite the positive movement, analysts caution that a lasting recovery is contingent upon significant improvements in the overall economic landscape. Additionally, India's merchandise trade deficit climbed to $30.21 billion in September, prompting concerns among investors about the impact of frequent foreign exchange regulations on market stability. ANI The Indian rupee rose 2% this week to post its biggest weekly gain in seven months, buoyed by policy measures aimed at boosting the currency, though analysts reckon a sustained turnaround hinges on aneasing of underlying strains. The currency closed at 94.96 per dollar, up 0.1% on the day. It recovered after threatening to breach its record low of 96.96 hit last week. Policymakers have moved to support the rupee by redirecting oil dollar demand away from the market, raising the cost of buying protection against a weaker rupee and slashing the limit for dollar purchases without underlying documentation proving exposures by 95% to $5 million. Traders and analysts said that the measures are likely to sap depreciation pressure in the near to medium term, but a meaningful recovery without central bank interventions would require a broader shift in conditions. "Our view is that, unless oil prices collapse, USD-INR faces upward pressure over time due to India's wider current account deficit, inflation differential, lack of catalyst for portfolio inflows, and the RBI's short FX forward position," Joey Chew, head of Asia FX research at HSBC, said in a note. Live Events "But we have also been thinking that the pair can be capped in the near term," he said, adding that he expects the rupee to weaken to 96 by year-end and 98 by the end of 2027. The Reserve Bank of India has used up about half of the more than $140 billion mobilised through special measures to bolster its FX war chest, and it's net forward dollar liabilities stood at $200 billion at the end of August. India's merchandise trade deficit widened to $30.21 billion in September, up from $26.8 billion in August. Investors have also warned that frequent FX rule changes to shore up the rupee risk undermining policy predictability and fragmenting currency market liquidity. Cult.fit, the fitness services and active lifestyle platform, has received observations from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its proposed IPO, according to the market regulator’s website. The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to Rs 950 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 17.86 crore equity shares by existing shareholders. The company has not specified the price band or issue dates in the details provided. Cult.fit plans to use the proceeds from the fresh issue to repay or prepay certain borrowings, fund capital expenditure for new fitness centres, invest in its subsidiary Cultsport for new exclusive brand outlets, meet lease-related payments for existing centres, and finance brand marketing and business promotion. A portion will also be allocated to general corporate purposes. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-134996338,width-210,height-158,imgsize-54116,resizemode-75/rupee-rises-1-9-in-a-week-closes-below-95-per-dollarbr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com The rupee closed below 95 per dollar for the first time in 38 days as RBI measures curbed dollar demand and boosted sentiment. The Indian rupee extended its gain Friday to close at 94.96 a dollar, below the psychological 95-mark for the first time in 38 days, as the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) aggressive measures in defence of the local currency led to a massive reduction in dollar demand. The currency appreciated about 1.9% this week, making it the biggest weekly gain in seven months, traders said. The rupee opened the day at 94.71, much stronger than the previous close of 95.05, and gained further to 94.67 but corporate dollar demand at lower levels forced it to settle at 94.96 in a shallow market. The unit closed at 96.73 last week very close to the lifetime low 96.96 seen on May 20. The rupee was seen trading below 95 earlier in the week too but it closed decisively below that level Friday for the first time since September 8, 2026. "A rebound in risk assets alongside the Reserve Bank of India’s aggressive defense strategy provided strong tailwinds for the local currency this week," HDFC Securities senior research analysts Dilip Parmar said in a note. Live Events The forward premiums remained elevated on account of tight liquidity and high bond yields. "There was not much change in rates from yesterday's level," a treasury head with a private bank said. The trading volume in the forex market remained low as the central bank cracked down on speculative bets and shifted the dollar demand from state-owned oil retailers from the spot market. It has opened a separate window to meet the demand from Indian Oil Corp , Hindustan Petroleum Corp and Bharat Petroleum Corp from its foreign exchange reserves. "On the technical chart, spot USD/INR is expected to find immediate support near 94.70, with resistance capped around 95.50," Parmar said. Meanwhile, the dollar index was down 0.3% at 101.7, prompting most Asian currencies to firm up. Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now!
